modules.title: Rocq & Roll
modules.summary: Interactive theorem proving in Rocq, from basic definitions and proofs to the type safety of the Simply Typed Lambda Calculus.
modules.abstract: This course introduces Rocq, an interactive theorem prover used to formally specify and verify the correctness of logical statements and programs. Starting with basic definitions, inductive types, and proofs, we will gradually build up to formalizing the Simply Typed Lambda Calculus. Along the way, you will gain hands-on experience writing definitions and constructing machine-checked proofs using the SSReflect proof language.
outline: Introduction to Rocq: basic definitions, functions, and proofs
Inductive types, recursive functions, and proofs by induction
Simply Typed Lambda Calculus (STLC) in Rocq
Proving progress, preservation, and type safety of STLC
modules.prerequisites: Familiarity with introductory logic, including propositional and first-order predicate logic, is recommended. A preparatory handout will be shared with participants.
modules.setup: Bring a laptop with Rocq 9.0 and the stdpp library installed. Participants without a laptop are welcome to pair up during the hands-on sessions.

modules.title: Design of Type Systems
modules.summary: Type systems from foundational and practical perspectives: logic and safety, polymorphism, resource management, and refinement types.
modules.abstract: Robin Milner’s famous quote, “Well-typed programs don’t go wrong” speaks to the centrality of types in modern programming. In this module, we will explore the design of type systems from both a foundational and practical perspective. We will bridge abstract logical principles with the mechanics underlying the design and implementation of type systems in real-world languages. The lectures will cover (a) the relationship between types and formal logic, typing judgements, and safety; (b) polymorphism and generics; (c) types and resource management as exemplified in languages like Rust, and (d) refinement types and its various extensions that allow types to carry logical predicates enabling richer and more expressive program reasoning and verification capabilities.
modules.setup: No labs are scheduled, and no software installation is required. Recent versions of OCaml and Z3 are optional for participants who would like to try the demonstrations.

modules.title: Symbolic Verification of Security Protocols
modules.summary: Symbolic approaches to verifying security protocols, with take-home exercises between the first and second day.
modules.setup: The planned exercises do not require Tamarin or ProVerif.

modules.title: Concurrent Separation Logic
modules.summary: An introduction to concurrent separation logic, with examples and a glimpse of Iris.

modules.title: Runtime Systems and JIT Compilation
modules.summary: Runtime-system design and JIT optimisation, connecting program analysis to precise, efficient, and sound execution.
modules.abstract: Just-in-time (JIT) compilers offer novel ways to optimize programs based on their execution profile and have found significant usage in languages with managed runtimes. However, as JIT compilation directly affects the execution time of a program, precision-enhancement techniques from the static-analysis world seldom find way into these otherwise powerful systems. Under this backdrop, we would first understand how modern JIT compilers optimize code, in tiered runtime systems, using examples of program analysis aimed at enabling stack allocation of heap objects in Java. We would then understand techniques to not only allocate a large number of objects on stack (leading to reduced garbage collection and improved performance), but to also handle challenges posed by possible dynamism in real-world Java Virtual Machines. In particular, we would talk about AOT-analysis guided optimistic stack allocation, as well as the usage of speculative JIT information in improving the precision of statically computed results. All parts of the story would be bound by the over-arching goal of maintaining precision and efficiency, while being sound, during program execution.
modules.setup: Install OpenJDK on your laptop. Any version is suitable for this module.
